content.text: : infection of endocardium that typically affects 1+ valves
: male, >60yo, IVDU, poor dentition, structural heart disease (e.g., MVP,
rheumatic heart disease), congenital heart disease (e.g., bicuspid AV, VSD,
PDA), prior IE, indwelling IV, chronic hemodialysis, HIV⊕
▪︎rapid, fulminant progression; fatal within 6wks if left untreated
▪︎indolent infection; progresses slowly over weeks to months
▪︎S. aureus: acute clinical course; common in IVDU	▪︎
▪︎malaise, HA, myalgia/arthralgia, night sweats, abdominal pain, dyspnea
(new/change), HF, arrhythmias (suspect perivalvular abscess if new conduction delay)
erythematous macules on palms/soles (cutaneous septic emboli)
nodules on finger/toe pads caused by immune complex deposition (“Osler, ouch”)
: round retinal hemorrhages w/ pale centers
(visual loss, motor weakness, aphasia), intracerebral hemorrhage, abscess
blood cultures x3 from separate sites
: vegetations (hyperechoic), perivalvular abscess, new valvular regurgitation, prosthetic valve dehiscence (rocking)
TTE within 12h of presentation, repeat after TX completed
prior IE, new murmur, heart failure)
➀ microorganisms shown by culture/histology of vegetation
➁ features of active endocarditis present on histology
▪︎IE symptoms resolve in ≤4d of ABX therapy
▪︎no pathologic evidence of IE found at surgery or autopsy
: leukocytosis w/ left shift, ⇡ ESR/CRP, ⊕RF, anemia
: PVE, HF, uncontrolled IE, perivalvular extension/complications, fungal IE, high embolic risk
➀ presence of prosthetic valve or material
